name: Over-the-shoulder graphs
what: The camera pushes into one top corner and a see-through glass line graph pops up beside your head: the line climbs with a glowing head while the number counts up. It pulls back, pushes into the other top corner, and a related glass bar graph pops up there, its bars growing while the second number counts. Your head stays in front of the glass.
origin: MotionLab's own build after a design in Vibha Ramprakash's claude-video-effects (MIT), 2026-10-28
motion: The companion corner_push moves the video: over the length L (150 f) corner A (top-left) f0-f75 (push f0-f12, hold, pull f63-f75), corner B (top-right) f75-f150 (push f75-f87, pull f138-f150). f9-f21 the line graph pops up in the top-left area from 82 % and 40 px lower (slow end, a small overshoot, seen within 3 f) while its grid lines draw in; f15-f43 the line climbs with a glowing head and a fill under it, the number counting with the same S-curve; f43 the number pops (8 f) and the head sends out a ring every 20 f; a band of light crosses the glass f45-f61; f57-f64 it shrinks and fades (accelerating) before the pull. f84-f96 the bar graph pops up in the top-right area; f90-f118 its 7 bars grow one after another (10 f each, slow end with a small overshoot) while the number counts; the highest bar glows and breathes; f132-f139 it shrinks away before the pull. All of it follows L: the holds are L/2 - 0.8 s each

tracks.what: the glass line graph pops up in the top-left area

min_why: each corner needs its push (0.4 s), a hold of at least 1.2 s for its graph to pop up and count, and its pull (0.4 s)
